the immune system is altered in patients with EDs at both extremes of the BMI range.
the serum levels of several cytokines and growth factor were altered in patients with AN and BED, and that these alterations are associated with EDs, BMI and eating behavior.

the identification of the role of cytokines and growth in EDs and their relationship with eating behaviors, which may help the understanding of the pathogenesis of the disorder.
a better understanding of the role of immune system in EDs and obesity, as well as the relationship between immune system and eating behaviors.

cytokine levels in EDs depend on ED type and severity and are also influenced by comorbid depression and eating behaviors.

the immune system in AN patients is characterized by a low-grade inflammatory state, while in obesity, the immune system appears to be more active, and this is not linked to depression, but to eating behaviors.

cytokines and growth factor alterations in EDs depend on ED type, BMI and depressive comorbidity.
the cytokine and growth factors profile of individuals with AN and BED are not similar, but both differ from that of HCs.
the brain behavior immune interaction is altered in individuals with EDs and that cytokine balance is affected by BMI, depression, eating behaviors and EDs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cytokine alterations in AN are not only due to low BMI, but are also associated with the EDs per se.
the cytokine profile is altered in EDs and that this is not only a consequence of BMI extremes, as cytokine levels differ between AN and obesity, with or without BED.

the immune system in AN is characterized by the presence of proinflammatory (IL-1α and IL-8) and anti-inflammatory (IL-10 and EGF) factors, while the immune system of obese individuals is characterized by the predominance of anti-inflammatory (IL10) and pro-inflammatory (IFN-ɣ) cytokines.
